testing_points: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread

skillNames.center-spread: Mean, median, range, standard deviation; outliers

template.name: mean_median_change
techniques: median depends on position, mean on every value
effect of changing an extreme value
misconceptions: thinking any change moves the median

concept: Lowering the largest value lowers the mean (it uses every value); the median (the middle position) stays the same when the corrected value is still above the middle value.

stem: The test scores of 7 students are listed below.
The score $99$ was recorded incorrectly. The correct score is $86$.
question.prompt: After the score is corrected, how do the mean and the median change?

choices.label: A
choices.display: The mean stays the same, and the median decreases.
choices.why: The sum falls by $99 - 86 = 13$, so the mean falls by $\dfrac{13}{7}$ points, while the median stays $82$.
choices.rationale: Swaps the roles of the mean and median.

choices.label: B
choices.display: Both the mean and the median decrease.
choices.why: The median is the 4th of the 7 ordered scores, $82$, before and after the change, because $86$ is still greater than $82$.
choices.rationale: Assumes every change moves the median.

choices.label: C
choices.display: Neither the mean nor the median changes.
choices.why: The sum of the scores falls by $13$, so the mean falls from $\dfrac{583}{7}$ to $\dfrac{570}{7}$; only the median stays the same.
choices.rationale: Thinks one value cannot move the mean.

choices.label: D
choices.display: The mean decreases, and the median stays the same.

answer.label: D
answer.display: The mean decreases, and the median stays the same.

steps.title: One change, two measures
steps.caption: **Careful:** changing a score does not always change the median. The median uses **position**; the mean uses **every** value.

steps.title: The median uses position
steps.caption: With $7$ ordered scores the median $M$ is the 4th: $82$. The corrected score $86$ is still above it, so the 4th score does not change.

steps.title: The mean uses every value
steps.caption: **Shortcut:** no need to find either mean. The sum drops by $13$, so the mean drops by $\dfrac{13}{7}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.caption: The mean decreases; the median stays the same.

solution.keyIdea: The mean uses **every** value. The median depends only on the **middle position**, and here the corrected score is still above the middle.
solution.summary: The median is the 4th score, 82, before and after. The sum falls by 13, so the mean falls by 13/7, from 83.29 to 81.43 (rounded).

meta.description_lead: One score changes from 99 to 86. What happens to the mean and median?
